issues.description: Command name mismatch: registered as quickmarks_reload but sibling commands use singular-dash form (quickmark-save, bookmark-add).
issues.detail: The codebase's existing voice is quickmark-* and bookmark-* (singular, dashed). This patch introduces quickmarks-reload/bookmarks-reload (plural). Pick one and match the surrounding code. The feature file even tests :bookmarks-reload while the code registers quickmarks_reload -> quickmarks-reload. Match the existing convention or justify the break in the commit message.

issues.description: Two commands smuggled into one patch; should be two patches.
issues.detail: This does quickmarks_reload AND bookmarks_reload. They share a base class change, fine, but the command additions are independent and should be reviewable independently. THREE-PATCHES (well, two): the urlmarks.py refactor extracting reload(), then quickmark command, then bookmark command. Easier to bisect, easier to revert one without the other.

issues.description: Reload() races with in-flight save; no consideration of dirty in-memory state.
issues.detail: If the user added a quickmark and the save-manager hasn't flushed yet, reload() blows it away silently. No warning, no check, no docstring note. For a tool the user invokes manually this is probably fine, but the docstring should say 'discards unsaved changes' so the next maintainer doesn't have to read the code to find out.

issues.description: Test writes to bm_file twice without verifying the first write was actually loaded.
issues.detail: test_reload constructs BookmarkManager after the first write, then rewrites the file, then reloads. It asserts only the post-reload state. Good enough to prove reload() works, but a one-line assert on the pre-reload marks would catch a regression where __init__ silently stops loading and reload() happens to produce the right answer anyway.

Every other scenario in this feature file has a descriptive name ('Saving a quickmark', 'Loading a bookmark in a background tab'). The two new ones are bare 'Scenario:'. Match the file's voice. Cheap fix, no excuse to skip.

issues.description: GOOD-TASTE on the urlmarks.py refactor; the __init__ duplication was a special case waiting to be removed.
issues.detail: Extracting reload() and calling it from __init__ eliminates the duplicated parse loop. This is the small-but-correct shape: one code path for loading marks, used at construction and on demand. Note it for the record; this is the kind of change that should land.

review.summary: The patch does a real thing in a small diff and includes the GOOD-TASTE refactor of folding __init__'s parse loop into a reusable reload() — that part lands. But the command naming breaks the codebase's own singular-dash convention (quickmark-save vs quickmarks-reload), and the patch bundles two independent command additions that should be two patches for clean bisect/revert. Tests exist but are minimal and the feature scenarios are unnamed, breaking the file's voice. Reload() silently discards unsaved in-memory state without documenting that contract. NEEDS-WORK: fix the naming to match the surrounding code, split into separate command patches, name the scenarios, and note the discard-unsaved behavior in the docstring.
